Requirements: R-1, R-4
Plan row: TS-1

Obligations: OB-1-1, OB-1-2

## Given
- A code datasource with a run-unique name (`tc001-<random>`) that this case creates itself from the GITLAB_PROJECT link and waits to COMPLETED (P-code-full). The case deletes it at the end.
- Baseline read B0: raw HTTP GET of the datasource details (the SDK model drops unknown fields, so the field `last_reindex_triggered_at` is read from the raw JSON). B0 may be null or a value; record it. Client clock T0 is taken immediately before the trigger.

## When
1. Trigger a manual full reindex through the update call with `full_reindex=true, skip_reindex=false`; client clock T1 right after the call returns.
2. Poll the datasource until its status leaves in-progress and is COMPLETED (bounded timeout).
3. Read the details twice more (R1, R2) with an independent GET each.

## Then
1. `last_reindex_triggered_at` in R1 is present and differs from B0 (null counts as different; an unchanged value fails).
2. The R1 value lies inside the client-clock window [T0 minus tolerance, completion time]; it is not an arbitrary later value (trigger-time stamping is the decided oracle, AC-2 wording is not asserted).
3. R2 equals R1 (the value is persisted, not recomputed per response) and is not B0.

## Self-probe notes
- Discrimination: on unfixed code the manual path wrote no stamp, so Then 1 fails (value stays B0). A copy of an earlier response would not pass Then 3 across separate GETs.
- Fixtures do not precompute the result: the expected value is only a window from the client clock. Data is run-unique; no global counts.
- Then reads through a separate GET, not the response of the trigger call.
- Tolerance: server naive local time vs client clock zone is an open question (R-19/OQ-9); if the server zone differs the window check is recorded inconclusive for Then 2 and Then 1 and 3 still stand.
- Not a defect check on trigger-time implementation.
